samples.text:
The table shows the value of five kinds of goods which one country exported in 2010 and 2024, in billions of US dollars.

Overall, the total value of exports increased from $68.3 billion to $86.6 billion, which is a rise of 27%. Most categories went up but two categories went down.

In 2010, vehicles was the biggest export with $22.1 billion, and machinery was second with $18.4 billion. However, in 2024 machinery became the biggest with $27.9 billion, it increased by 52%. Vehicles fell to $19.6 billion, a decrease of 11%.

Pharmaceuticals had the biggest growth. The value was only $6.3 billion in 2010 but it rise to $16.8 billion in 2024, so the change was 167%. Food products also grew from $9.8 billion to $14.1 billion, which is 44% more.

On the other hand, textiles decreased the most. In 2010 it were $11.7 billion, but in 2024 it was only $8.2 billion, a fall of 30%, and it became the smallest category of exports in 2024.
samples.why: Overview present and all figures accurate · key changes identified but described mechanically · repetitive vocabulary (biggest, went up) · agreement errors, a comma splice and a verb-form error that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The table illustrates the value of a country's exports in five categories of goods in 2010 and 2024, together with the percentage change over this period.

Overall, the country's total exports grew significantly, rising by 27% from $68.3 billion to $86.6 billion. While three categories expanded, with pharmaceuticals experiencing by far the fastest growth, exports of vehicles and textiles declined.

In 2010, vehicles were the country's most valuable export, worth $22.1 billion, followed by machinery at $18.4 billion. By 2024, however, their positions had reversed, as machinery exports climbed by 52% to $27.9 billion, while vehicle exports decreased by 11% to $19.6 billion.

The most dramatic change was seen in pharmaceuticals, whose value rose from only $6.3 billion to $16.8 billion, an increase of 167%. As a result, pharmaceuticals overtook textiles and food products to become the third largest category. Food products also performed well, growing by 44% from $9.8 billion to $14.1 billion. Textiles, in contrast, saw the steepest fall of any category, dropping by 30% from $11.7 billion to $8.2 billion, which made it the smallest export category in 2024.
samples.why: Clear overview of overall growth and contrasting categories · changes in ranking highlighted · logical organisation · good range of vocabulary and linking · mostly error-free with slight repetition of category.

samples.text:
The table compares the value, in billions of US dollars, of five categories of goods exported by one country in 2010 and 2024, alongside the percentage change in each.

Although the country's export earnings rose substantially overall, the categories performed very differently. Machinery replaced vehicles as the leading export, pharmaceuticals grew at a remarkable rate, and textiles and vehicles were the only categories to shrink.

Total exports increased by 27%, from $68.3 billion to $86.6 billion. Machinery expanded by $9.5 billion, or 52%, to reach $27.9 billion. Vehicles, by contrast, had been the most valuable category in 2010, at $22.1 billion, but their value fell by 11% to $19.6 billion, pushing them into second place.

Pharmaceuticals recorded the most spectacular growth, with exports rising by 167%, from $6.3 billion to $16.8 billion. This gain of $10.5 billion, the largest of any category in absolute terms as well, lifted the sector from the smallest category to the third largest. Food products also grew steadily, by 44%, to $14.1 billion. Textiles, however, suffered the sharpest decline, losing almost a third of their value as exports dropped from $11.7 billion to $8.2 billion, leaving them the smallest category by 2024.
samples.why: Clear overview capturing the change of leader and contrasting trends · absolute and relative changes integrated accurately · cohesion well managed · precise vocabulary · wide range of structures, error-free.
